STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r12.claim: Verses 4–31 reject the Makkans' excuses and recall earlier peoples destroyed for ignoring messengers, previewing the rejecters' fate in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r12.anchor: After rejecting the Makkans’ excuses for not heeding the warning of the Prophet Muhammad, the sūrah continues with a reminder of the fate that befell previous generations

BURSEVI:v3p18/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18/r1.claim: The vocative of regret is figurative hyperbole: they call regret to arrive now, like calling woe, highlighting their foolish past choices.
BURSEVI:v3p18/r1.anchor: ونداؤها مجاز لأن الحسرة لا يتأتى منها الإقبال وإنما المعنى على المبالغة في شدة التحسر

BURSEVI:v3p18/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18/r2.claim: They regret neglecting the Hour, failing to believe in it and prepare through good deeds; tafrīṭ means leaving what one could have done.
BURSEVI:v3p18/r2.anchor: على تفريطنا في شأن الساعة وتقصيرنا في مراعاة حقها والاستعداد لها بالإيمان بها

BURSEVI:v3p18/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18/r3.claim: The clause about carrying burdens describes their state as they speak; awzār are sins named as heavy loads.
BURSEVI:v3p18/r3.anchor: {وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم} حال من فاعل قالوا ، والأوزار جمع وزر

BURSEVI:v3p18/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18/r4.claim: Calling sins loads and placing them on backs is metaphor, since burdens belong to bodies; backs are mentioned because people ordinarily carry weight there.
BURSEVI:v3p18/r4.anchor: والحمل من توابع الأعيان الكثيفة لا من عوارض المعاني فلا يوصف به العرض إلا على سبيل التمثيل والتشبيه

BURSEVI:v3p18/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18/r5.claim: The contrast is that they mourn the good deeds they failed to do while physically bearing the sins they did commit.
BURSEVI:v3p18/r5.anchor: والمعنى أنهم يتحسرون على ما لم يعملوا من الحسنات والحال إنهم يحملون أوزار ما عملوا من السيئات

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r1.claim: The closing phrase means how evil a load they bear.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r1.anchor: {ألا سآء ما يزرون} أي : بئس شيئا يزرون ، أي : يحملون وزرهم.

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r2.speaker: السدي وغيره
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and others report that a believer meets a beautiful, fragrant form of his good deeds after rising and rides it, as in the gathering of the God-conscious as mounted guests.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r2.anchor: قال السدي وغيره : إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أحسن شيء صورة وأطيبه ريحا

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r3.speaker: السدي وغيره
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r3.claim: The unbeliever instead meets an ugly, foul-smelling embodiment of evil deeds that says it rode him in life and now rides him.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r3.anchor: وأما الكافر : فيستقبله أقبح شيء صورة وأنتنه ريحا

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r4.claim: On this report, carrying deeds is literal because deeds take visible forms in the afterlife although they are accidents here.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r4.anchor: فيكون الحمل على حقيقته لأن للأعمال صورا تظهر في الآخرة وإن كان نفسها إعراضا

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r5.claim: Existence itself is the greatest burden because it gives rise to other sins and blocks the seeker; repent of all and efface the self in the path of truth.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r5.anchor: ذنب الوجود فوق الكل ؛ إذ هو الباعث على سائر الأوزار وهو ثقل مانع عن السلوك

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r6.speaker: حافظ
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r6.claim: Hafez’s verse rejects self-centered thought and opinion in the world of spiritual freedom, treating self-regard as unbelief in that path.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r6.anchor:
فكر خود ورأى خود در عالم رندى نيست
كفرست درين مذهب خود بيني وخودر رأيي

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r7.claim: Some say one cannot escape the self by means of the self; only God enables release.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r7.anchor: لا يمكن الخروج من النفس بالنفس وإنما يمكن الخروج من النفس بالله تعالى

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r8.speaker: الشيخ أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي الترمذي الحكيم
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r8.claim: Al-Tirmidhi teaches that remembrance moistens and softens the heart; without it, ego and desire harden it and the limbs resist obedience like a dead tree fit for cutting.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r8.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى يرطب القلب ويلينه فإذا خلا عن الذكر أصابته حرارة النفس ونار الشهوات فقسا ويبس

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r9.speaker: الشيخ أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي الترمذي الحكيم
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r9.claim: Remembrance, divine unity, and following their people are the foundations of spiritual life.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r9.anchor: فالذكر والتوحيد والاتباع إلى أهله هو أصل الأصول

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r10.speaker: علي بن الموفق
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r10.claim: Ali ibn al-Muwaffaq dreamed that heavenly maidens washed his feet after he gave up his litter and joined other pilgrims on foot; they counted him among them because he loved their company.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r10.anchor: حججت سنة من السنين في محمل فرأيت رجالا ، فأحببت المشي معهم فنزلت وأركبت واحدا في المحمل

BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r11.claim: The story teaches that sound-hearted companionship with a saint benefits; following and hearing the Prophet could remove deniers’ burdens and lead them to Paradise, though God guides whom He wills.
BURSEVI:v3p18#2/r11.anchor: هذه حال من مشى مع ولي باعتقاد صحيح فكيف مع نبي فلو أن كفار مكة ومشركي العرب استمعوا إلى النبي

QASHANI:6:31-33/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:31-33/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:31-33/r1.claim: The losers are veiled deniers of meeting the Real; the minor resurrection brings regret for neglect, while their burdens comprise attachments, bodily love, sins, and sensory traits rooted in their souls.
QASHANI:6:31-33/r1.anchor: القيامة الصغرى ندموا على تفريطهم فيها

QASHANI:6:31-33/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:31-33/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:31-33/r2.claim: Carrying burdens on their backs means the traits have rooted in the soul, veiling and tormenting them and restraining their aims.
QASHANI:6:31-33/r2.anchor: أي: ارتكبتهم واستولت عليهم للرسوخ في نفوسهم فحجبتهم وعذبتهم وثبطتهم

AKHFASH:v1p297/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p297/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p297/r1.claim: يزرون derives from وزر يزر وزرا; the form وزر فهو موزور is also used.
AKHFASH:v1p297/r1.anchor: وقال {ألا سآء ما يزرون} لأنه من "وزر" "يزر" [109 ء] "وزرا" ويقال أيضا: "وزر" ف"هو موزور".

AKHFASH:v1p297/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p297/r2.speaker: يونس
AKHFASH:v1p297/r2.claim: Yunus says both وزر and وزر are used.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p152#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p152#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p152#6/r1.claim: أوزارهم means their sins; the root word الوزر is a load carried on the back, as in God removing a burden that weighed heavily.

NAHHAS:v2p62/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p62/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p62/r5.claim: They lost their deeds and their reward; بغتة is accusative circumstantial, a verbal noun functioning as a state like قتله صبرا.
NAHHAS:v2p62/r5.anchor: أي قد خسروا أعمالهم وثوابها ( حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة ) نصب على الحال وهي عند سيبويه مصدر

NAHHAS:v2p62/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p62/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p62/r6.claim: Sibawayh cites an anonymous poem with لأيا بلأي as a circumstantial verbal noun but says this usage cannot be generalized to جاء فلان سرعة.
NAHHAS:v2p62/r6.anchor: وأنشد ( فلأيا بلأي ما حملنا وليدنا … على ظهر محبوك ظماء مفاصلة ) ولا يجيز سيبويه أن يقاس عليه

NAHHAS:v2p62/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p62/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p62/r7.claim: أوزار means sins made heavy like a load on the back; another view takes it as punishments, also called a burden.
NAHHAS:v2p62/r7.anchor: وهم يحملون أوزارهم ) أي ذنوبهم جعلها لثقلها بمنزلة الحمل الثقيل

NAHHAS:v2p62/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p62/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p62/r8.claim: A second explanation says the loads are punishments, since punishment is also called wizr; يزرون means they carry.
NAHHAS:v2p62/r8.anchor: وقيل يعني عقوبات الذنوب لأن العقوبة يقال لها وزر ( ألا ساء ما يزرون ) أي يحملون

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ، أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r1.claim: God reminds the denier of meeting Him of His gifts; the servant admits having forgotten God.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة يبلغ به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : يلقى العبد يوم القيامة ، فيقول : اي فل . الم اكرمك واسودك وازوجك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ، أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r2.claim: The Hour may arrive while a person is eating or two people are trading and cannot finish.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : تقوم الساعة على رجل اكلته في فيه يلوكها ولا يسيغها

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r3.claim: The Hour will not come until a caller announces it three times.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة انه قال : لا تقوم الساعة حتى ينادي مناد : يا ايها الناسن اتتكم الساعة ، اتتكم الساعة ، اتتكم الساعة . ثلاثا .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r4.claim: The regret is seeing the people of Hell lose their places in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r4.anchor: عن الاعمش ، عن أبي سعيد قال : رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : يا حسرتنا قال : الحسرة يرى اهل النار منازلهم من الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r5.claim: The cry of حسرة means regret.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس في قوله : يا حسرة قال : الندامة .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r6.claim: They regret having neglected deeds that would earn Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r6.anchor: عن السدى قوله : على ما فرطنا فيها ، اما فرطنا فضيعنا من عمل الجنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r7.claim: Their regret stems from having mocked the messengers.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد : يا حسرة قال : كانت عليهم حسرة استهزاؤهم بالرسل .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r8.speaker: أبو مرزوق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r8.claim: A sinner meets his foul deed in human form at the grave and is carried by it into Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1280#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي مرزوق قال : ويستقبل الكافر أو الفاجر عند خروجه من قبره كاقبح صورة راها ، وانتنها ريحا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r1.claim: An evil deed appears as an ugly, foul grave-companion, then rides its bearer into the Fire on Resurrection Day.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r1.anchor: عن السدى قوله : يحملون اوزارهم على ظهورهم ، فانه ليس من رجل ظالم يموت ، فيدخل قبره الا جاءه رجل قبيح الوجه اسود اللون ، منتن الريح

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r2.claim: The burdens they carry are their deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1281/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : الا ساء ما يزرون قال : ما يعملون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r1.claim: This resumption marvels at the disbelievers' end: denial of resurrection emboldened persistent disbelief, which brings punishment and justifies saying they have lost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r1.anchor: استئناف للتعجيب من حالهم حين يقعون يوم القيامة في العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r2.claim: Their loss here is deprivation of the afterlife's good, not worldly loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r2.anchor: والخسارة هنا حرمان خيرات الآخرة لا الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r3.claim: Those denying the meeting of God are the people just quoted as saying that only worldly life exists; explicit naming, rather than a pronoun, makes the statement independent and develops their fate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r3.anchor: والذين كذبوا بلقاء الله هم الذين حكي عنهم بقوله : وقالوا إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r4.claim: Meeting God means the afterlife's unimpeded manifestation of divine approval and wrath; it is a representational metaphor comparing judgment to servants meeting their lord after absence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r4.anchor: فلما كان العالم الأخروي وهو ما بعد البعث عالم ظهور الحقائق بآثارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r5.claim: In worldly life, God could punish people at once but delays, warns, and promises while they choose obedience or sin; in the next life effects appear without delay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r5.anchor: فإذا طوي هذا العالم وجاءت الحياة الثانية صار الناس في نظام آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r6.claim: The meeting metaphor is common in Quran and Prophetic speech; he cites the hadith about loving to meet God and the day called the meeting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p188/r6.anchor: وشاع هذا التمثيل في القرآن وكلام الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r1.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r1.claim: Hatta before idha is initial and indicates causation, effectively meaning when the hour comes, rather than an endpoint.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r1.anchor: كما صرح به ابن الحاجب ، أي فإذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r2.claim: Some commentators make the hour the endpoint of loss, but the author rejects this because the loss in question is at the Resurrection and not everyone suffered worldly loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r2.anchor: ومن المفسرين من جعل مجيء الساعة غاية للخسران ، وهو فاسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r3.claim: Al-sa'a is the conventional proper name for the hour of resurrection and gathering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r3.anchor: والساعة : علم بالغلبة على ساعة البعث والحشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r4.claim: Baghtatan derives from sudden surprise without warning or any sign; its accusative is a circumstantial source noun, giving the report emphatic force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r4.anchor: والبغتة فعلة من البغت ، وهو مصدر بغته الأمر إذا نزل به فجأة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r5.claim: The clause they said answers idha; ya hasratana personifies regret and calls it to arrive at the moment of remorse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r5.anchor: قالوا } جواب ( إذا ) . و { يا حسرتنا } نداء مقصود به التعجب والتندم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r6.claim: They attach regret to themselves because they lament their own fate; a bare call to regret more often laments others, while ya hasrata makes ala refer to the cause of regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p189/r6.anchor: وأضافوا الحسرة إلى أنفسهم ليكون تحسرهم لأجل أنفسهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r1.claim: The opening is a fresh report of the deniers’ loss that magnifies their calamity; choosing disbelief while discarding faith resembles a failed exchange, and the allusion is to those who say only worldly life exists.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r1.anchor: هذا استئناف إخبار عن خسارة المكذبين يتضمن تعظيم المصاب الذي حل بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r2.claim: Meeting God means returning to Him and to His judgment and power, like meeting the consequences and outcome of one’s deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r2.anchor: بلقاء الله معناه: بالرجوع إليه وإلى أحكامه وقدرته، كما تقول لقي فلان أعماله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r3.claim: The Hour has a definite article without prior mention because it is famous and established in people’s minds and is also implied by meeting God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r3.anchor: والساعة يوم القيامة، وأدخل عليها تعريف العهد دون تقدم ذكرها لشهرتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r4.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly; it is an accusative verbal noun used circumstantially, a construction Sibawayh does not allow by analogy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r4.anchor: وبغتة معناه فجأة، تقول بغتني الأمر أي فجأني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r5.claim: Calling out regret magnifies the event: the speaker figuratively calls it to come or appear, stirring both speaker and listener, as when addressing a house, quarter, or animal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r5.anchor: ونداء الحسرة على تعظيم الأمر وتشنيعه، قال سيبويه وكأن الذي ينادي الحسرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r6.claim: Farraṭnā means falling short despite having the ability not to; the pronoun in fīhā may refer to the Hour, the implied bargain, or worldly life, with different contextual senses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r6.anchor: وفرطنا معناه قصرنا مع القدرة على ترك التقصير، وهذه حقيقة التفريط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r7.speaker: الحسن والطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan refers the pronoun to the Hour, meaning they neglected preparation for it; al-Tabari refers it to the transaction implied by the opening loss, while worldly life is another possible antecedent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p283#2/r7.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن، وقال الطبري يعود على الصفقة التي يتضمنها ذكر الخسارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r1.claim: The circumstantial waw introduces their carrying; awzār is the plural of wizr, a burden of sins, with related Arabic forms and a prophetic expression maʾzūrāt ghayr maʾjūrāt explained by Abu ʿAli as sound-following.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r1.anchor: والأوزار جمع وزر بكسر الواو وهو الثقل من الذنوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r2.claim: The burden is figurative and placed on the back to intensify the image; deriving wizr from a refuge mountain or wazīr-helper is unclear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r2.anchor: والوزر هنا تجوز وتشبيه بثقل الأحمال، وقوى التشبيه بأن جعله على الظهور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r3.claim: Al-Tabari and others take the carrying literally: each person’s deed appears in a form, the believer’s beautiful and fragrant and the disbeliever’s ugly and foul, and the image of the deed is carried on the back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r3.anchor: وقال الطبري وغيره هذا على جهة الحقيقة ورووا في ذلك خبرا أن المؤمن يلقاه عمله في أحسن صورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r4.claim: Alā announces and publicizes the gravity of what follows, as in Prophetic calls to convey and witness; sāʾa is a plain report or may function like biʾsa with mā as its subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r4.anchor: إخبار عن سوء ما يأثمون مضمن التعظيم لذلك والإشادة به، وهذا كقول النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r5.claim: The grammar of sāʾa may be a past verb with mā as its subject, as in a poetic example, or may follow the construction of biʾsa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p284/r5.anchor: وساء فعل ماض وما فاعلة به كما تقول ساءني أمر كذا، ويحتمل أن تجري ساء هنا مجرى بئس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r1.claim: They are called losers because they exchanged faith for unbelief; meeting God means resurrection and recompense, the Hour is the Resurrection, and baghta means suddenly, as al-Zajjaj’s poetry illustrates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r1.anchor: لأنهم باعوا الإيمان بالكفر فعظم خسرانهم والمراد بلقاء الله البعث والجزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r2.claim: Hasra is grief over something lost; exegetes gloss the cry as “our regret.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r2.anchor: الحسرة التلهف على الشيء الفائت وأهل التفسير يقولون يا ندامتنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r3.claim: Calling out to an inanimate regret is an Arabic device for forceful emphasis: the intended audience is onlookers, not regret itself; parallels include “O horses of God, ride,” as Sibawayh explains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r3.anchor: إذا اجتهدت في المبالغة في الإخبار عن عظيم ما تقع فيه جعلته نداء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r4.claim: Tafriṭ means wasting or neglecting; al-Zajjaj also glosses it as delay caused by incapacity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r4.anchor: فأما التفريط فهو التضييع وقال الزجاج التفريط في اللغة تقدمه العجز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r5.claim: The pronoun in “in it” may refer to this worldly life, meaning they neglected afterlife deeds there, according to Muqatil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r5.anchor: أنها الدنيا فالمعنى على ما ضيعنا في الدنيا من عمل الآخرة قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir says the pronoun refers to an unstated transaction, since loss only occurs in a transaction and the context makes it understood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r6.anchor: أنها الصفقة لأن الخسران لا يكون إلا في صفقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r7.claim: Some exegetes take the pronoun to refer to obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r7.anchor: والثالث أنها الطاعة ذكره بعض المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says awzār are sins, with the root sense of a load on the back; Ibn Faris likewise defines wizr as weight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r8.anchor: هي الآثام واصل الوزر الحمل على الظهر وقال ابن فارس الوزر الثقل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r9.speaker: عمير بن هانئ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r9.claim: One view takes the carrying literally: ʿUmayr ibn Haniʾ describes each unbeliever’s deed appearing as an ugly man that mounts him and exposes him publicly; al-Suddi, ʿAmr ibn Qays, and Muqatil also hold this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p24#3/r9.anchor: يحشر مع كل كافر عمله في صورة رجل قبيح كلما كان هول عظمه عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says carrying the burdens is figurative: the weight of their sins, with punishment treated as the heaviest thing they could bear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r1.anchor: أنه مثل والمعنى يحملون ثقل ذنوبهم قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r2.claim: “How evil is what they carry” means how vile a burden they bear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p26/r2.anchor: بئس الشيء شيئا يزرونه أي يحملونه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r1.claim: Those denying encounter with God lose and will suddenly regret wasted deeds and their prior bad actions when the Hour arrives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن خسارة من كذب بلقاء الله وعن خيبته إذا جاءته الساعة بغتة، وعن ندامته على ما فرط من العمل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in the regret about what was neglected may refer to worldly life, deeds, or the afterlife and its affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الضمير يحتمل عوده على الحياة [الدنيا] (7) وعلى الأعمال، وعلى الدار الآخرة، أي: في أمرها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r3.claim: The wording about carrying burdens means carrying them; Qatada also glosses the verb as working or earning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r3.anchor: وقوله {وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون} أي: يحملون. وقال قتادة: يعملون.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r4.speaker: أبو مرزوق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r4.claim: Abu Marzuq describes a wicked person meeting an ugly, foul-smelling embodiment of his evil deeds at resurrection; it rides him toward Hell, illustrating the burdens on their backs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي مرزوق قال: ويستقبل الكافر -أو: الفاجر - (9) -عند خروجه من قبره كأقبح صورة رآها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says an unjust dead person is accompanied in the grave by an ugly, black, stinking figure that embodies his deeds; at resurrection he carries it toward the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p249#2/r5.anchor: وقال أسباط: عن السدي أنه قال: ليس من رجل ظالم يموت فيدخل قبره إلا جاءه رجل قبيح الوجه

JISHUMI:v3p2205/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r4.claim: Loss means diminution or destruction; its central idea is decrease, though some say its origin is destruction.
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r4.anchor: وأصل الباب: النقصان، وقيل: أصله الهلاك

JISHUMI:v3p2205/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r5.claim: Meeting primarily means encountering or facing someone, then by extension seeing; it can also mean living in the same era or encountering calamity and battle without literal sight.
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r5.anchor: وكل شيء صادف شيئا، أو استقبله فقد لقيه، تقول: لقيت فلانا

JISHUMI:v3p2205/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r6.claim: Baghtatan means sudden arrival without the person knowing when it will occur.
JISHUMI:v3p2205/r6.anchor: والبغتة: الفجأة، وهو ورود الشيء على [صاحبه بغير] علمه بوقته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r1.claim: Standing before the Lord is a metaphor for detention and rebuke like a guilty servant before his master; alternatives say they encounter His recompense or recognize Him fully.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r1.anchor: مجاز على الحبس للتوبيخ والسؤال ، كما يوقف العبد الجاني بين يدي سيده ليعاتبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r2.claim: ‘Is this not the truth?’ answers an imagined question about God’s words and rebukes their denial of resurrection and recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r2.anchor: وهذا تعيير من الله تعالى لهم على التكذيب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r3.claim: They taste punishment because they disbelieved in meeting God and the afterlife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r3.anchor: بكفركم بلقاء الله ببلوغ الآخرة وما يتصل بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r4.claim: Ḥattā ends their denial, not their loss, which has no endpoint; denial continued until the Hour brought regret.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r4.anchor: غاية لكذبوا لا لخسر ، لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r5.claim: Death is the start of the afterlife and its preliminaries, so it counts as part of the Hour.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r5.anchor: لما كان الموت وقوعا في أحوال الآخرة ومقدماتها جعل من جنس الساعة وسمي باسمها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever dies has begun his resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r6.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 373 ) ( من مات فقد قامت قيامته )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, the Hour follows death so quickly that it is like an unexpected strike.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r7.anchor: أو جعل مجيء الساعة بعد الموت لسرعته كالوقاع بغير فترة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r8.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly, either as a circumstantial adverb or an absolute verbal noun emphasizing surprise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r8.anchor: { بغتة } فجأة وانتصابها على الحال بمعنى باغتة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r9.claim: ‘We neglected it’ refers to worldly life, understood from context, or to the Hour and belief in it, as in ‘I neglected God’s side.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r9.anchor: الضمير للحياة الدنيا ، جيء بضميرها وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لكونها معلومة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r10.claim: Their sins are carried on their backs as burdens are customarily carried there; the wording compares this with deeds of the hands in 42:30.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r10.anchor: لأنه اعتيد حمل الأثقال على الظهور ، كما ألف الكسب بالأيدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r11.claim: ‘Evil is what they bear’ means their burden is a wretched thing, like the construction in 7:177.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p17#3/r11.anchor: بئس شيئا يزرون وزرهم ، كقوله { ساء مثلا القوم }

MUQATIL:6:31/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:31/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:31/r1.claim: Quraysh disbelievers will suddenly face the Resurrection and lament neglecting God’s remembrance; their evil deeds appear as an ugly, foul-smelling figure that demands they carry it, then rides their backs.
MUQATIL:6:31/r1.anchor: أتاه عمله الخبيث فى صورة حبشى، أشوه، منتن الريح، كريه المنظر،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r1.claim: Meeting God can mean reaching the afterlife and what follows, or can be taken literally, since denying resurrection also denies vision of God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r1.anchor: ببلوغ الآخرة وما يتصل بها أو هو مجرى على ظاهره لأن منكر البعث منكر للرؤية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r2.claim: The endpoint particle reaches the coming of the Hour, not their loss, which has no end.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ حتى ﴾ غاية لكذبوا لا لخسر لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r3.claim: The Hour is the Resurrection; its delayed arrival followed by eternity makes its intervening duration like one hour.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r3.anchor: أى القيامة لأن مدة تأخرها مع تأبد ما بعدها كساعة واحدة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r4.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly and may be parsed as a circumstantial accusative or cognate accusative, the hour arriving without warning of its time.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r4.anchor: فجأة وانتصابها على الحال يعنى باغتة أو على المصدر كأنه قيل بغتتهم الساعة بغتة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r5.claim: The exclamation personifies regret, calling it to come because its time has arrived.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r5.anchor: نداء تفجع معناه يا حسرة احضرى فهذا أوانك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r6.claim: They regret neglecting either worldly life or the Hour itself by failing to prepare for or believe in it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r6.anchor: ﴿ على ما فرطنا ﴾ قصرنا ﴿ فيها ﴾ فى الحياة الدنيا أو فى الساعة أى قصرنا فى شأنها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r7.claim: Their sins on their backs uses the familiar image of carrying heavy things; it figuratively means sin clings to them without leaving.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r7.anchor: خص الظهر لأن المعهود حمل الأثقال على الظهور كما عهد الكسب بالأيدى وهو مجاز عن اللزوم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r8.claim: A report depicts the dead person's ugly deed as a foul-smelling figure: it says the person rode it in life, and now it rides him.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r8.anchor: وقيل أن الكافر إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أقبح شيء صورة وأخبثه ريحا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r9.claim: The particle ألا intensifies the severity of what is said next.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p319#4/r9.anchor: وأفاد ألا تعظيم ما يذكر بعده

SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r1.claim: Baghtatan has four parses: circumstantial from the subject or object, a cognate-like verbal noun for ‘they surprised them,’ an implied verb from the same root, or an implied verb meaning ‘they came.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { بغتة }: في نصبها أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أنها مصدر في موضع الحال من فاعل " جاءتهم " أي: مباغتة،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r2.claim: Baght and baghtatan mean a sudden, rapid event without anticipating or attending to it; even an expected event is not baghtatan merely because it arrives quickly.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r2.anchor: والبغت والبغتة مفاجأة الشيء بسرعة من غير اعتداد به ولا جعل بال منه

SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r3.claim: A poetic line illustrates the strict sense of baghtatan as wholly unanticipated suddenness.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r3.anchor: ولذلك قال الشاعر: 1898- إذا بغتت أشياء قد كان قبلها قديما فلا تعتدها بغتات

SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r4.claim: The article in al-sāʿa is the article of a uniquely famous referent, as in ‘the star’ and al-Thurayya.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r4.anchor: والألف واللام في " الساعة " للغلبة كالنجم والثريا، لأنها غلبت على يوم القيامة،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r5.claim: The Hour is called al-sāʿa because reckoning there is swift.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r5.anchor: وسميت القيامة ساعة لسرعة الحساب فيها على الباري تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31/r6.claim: ‘They said’ is the answer to idhā.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r1.claim: Calling ‘O our regret’ is metaphorical because regret cannot literally be summoned; it magnifies their anguish as if they called regret at its appointed moment, like ‘woe to me.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r1.anchor: هذا مجاز، لأن الحسرة لا يتأتى منها الإقبال، وإنما المعنى على المبالغة في شدة التحر،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r2.claim: The call also rebukes them for neglecting what made them need to summon regret and woe.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r2.anchor: والمقصود التنبيه على خطأ المنادي حيث ترك ما أحوجه تركه إلى نداء هذه الأشياء

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r3.claim: ‘For what we neglected’ attaches to regret, and mā is a verbal noun: ‘for our neglect.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r3.anchor: و " ما " مصدرية، أي: على تفريطنا.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r4.claim: The pronoun in ‘in it’ may refer to the Hour, with an implied matter of the Hour and belief in it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يعود على الساعة، ولا بد من مضاف أي: في شأنها والإيمان بها،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says ‘in it’ refers to the transaction implied by the statement that they lost.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r5.anchor: وأن يعود على الصفقة المتضمنة في قوله: { قد خسر الذين } قاله الحسن،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the pronoun to refer to worldly life, though it has not been mentioned, because it is understood.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r6.anchor: لها ذكر لكونها معلومة، قاله الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r7.claim: A proposed reference to their places in Paradise when they see them is remote.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: يعود على مازلهم في الجنة إذا رأوها. وهو بعيد.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r8.claim: Tafrīṭ is falling short in something one can do.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r8.anchor: والتفريط: التقصير في الشيء مع القدرة على فعله.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses tafrīṭ as wasting or neglecting.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r10.speaker: ابن بحر
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r10.claim: Ibn Bahr derives tafrīṭ from ‘preceding’: to let another take the lead; the doubled form is privative, like the expression for skinning a camel.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: " هو السبق، منه الفارط أي السابق للقوم، فمعنى فرط بالتشديد خلى السبق لغيره،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r11.claim: The author compares the privative use with ‘make night prayer an extra,’ cited at 17:79.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#2/r11.anchor: فالتضعيف فيه للسلب كجلدت البعير ومنه فتهجد به نافلة

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r1.claim: The wāw in ‘while they carry’ marks a circumstantial clause whose subject is the pronoun in ‘they said.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r1.anchor: الواو للحال، وصاحب الحال الواو في " قالوا " أي: قالوا: يا حسرتنا في حالة حملهم أوزارهم.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r2.claim: Repeating the explicit pronoun at the start of the clause is more emphatic.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r2.anchor: وصدرت هذه الجملة بضمير مبتدأ ليكون ذكره مرتين فهو أبلغ

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r3.claim: Carrying the burdens may be metaphor for enduring punishment caused by their sins, or literal carrying.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r3.anchor: والحمل هنا قيل: مجاز عن مقاساتهم العذاب الذي سببه الأوزار، وقيل: هو حقيقة.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r4.claim: A hadith says a person’s deed is represented as an ugly, foul-smelling image that he carries.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث: " إنه يمثل له عمله بصورة قبيحة منتنة الريح فيحملها "

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r5.claim: The back is specified because it bears more than other body parts, like the head and nape; this parallels the hand’s stronger touch in 6:7.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r5.anchor: وخص الظهر لأنه يطيق من الحمل ما لا يطيقه غيره من الأعضاء كالرأس والكاهل

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r6.claim: Awzār is the plural of wizr, on patterns such as ḥaml/aḥmāl and ʿadl/aʿdāl.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r6.anchor: الأوزار: جمع وزر كحمل وأحمال وعدل وأعدال.

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r7.claim: The root’s basic sense is weight; wazartuhu means I loaded him with something heavy.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r7.anchor: والوزر في الأصل الثقل، ومنه: وزرته أي: حملته شيئا ثقيلا،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r8.claim: The title wazīr comes from bearing the burdens of governing the king’s subjects and household.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r8.anchor: ووزير الملك من هذا لأنه يتحمل أعباء ما قلده الملك من مؤونة رعيته وحشمته

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r9.claim: Awzār al-ḥarb means the weapons and equipment of war, as a poetic line illustrates.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r9.anchor: ومنه أوزار الحرب لسلاحها وآلاتها، قال:

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r10.claim: Another etymology starts from wazar, a mountain refuge (75:11), then extends to weight by simile and sin by the hardship it brings; the root connotes heaviness and protection.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#3/r10.anchor: وقيل: الأصل في ذلك الوزر بفتح الواو الزاي، وهو الملجأ الذي يلتجأ إليه من الجبل،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r1.claim: Sāʾa may be a transitive, inflected verb with an omitted object and mā as subject; mā can be relative, verbal, or an indefinite description, with an understood referent where needed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها " ساء " المتصرفة المتعدية، ووزنها حينئذ فعل فتح العين، ومفعولها حينئذ محذوف،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya begins with the plain declarative reading, like ‘this pleased me badly’; the author notes the poem’s mā could still have several analyses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r2.anchor: وبدأ ابن عطية بهذا الوجه قال: " كما تقول: ساءني هذا الأمر، والكلام خبر مجرد كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r3.claim: The Shaykh says mā in the poem cannot be fixed as a bare declarative; all three grammatical possibilities remain open.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يتعين أن تكون " ما " في البيت خبرا مجردا

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r4.claim: A second reading makes sāʾa an exclamation, with ḍamma on the second radical, meaning ‘how awful what they carry!’
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r4.anchor: أن تكون للتعجب فتنتقل من فعل بفتح العين إلى فعل بضمها

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r5.claim: A third reading makes sāʾa equivalent to biʾsa, an intensified form of blame; the construction follows the discussion of mā in 2:90.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r5.anchor: أنها بمعنى بئس فتكون للمبالغة في الذم

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r6.claim: The first reading is transitive, flexible, and declarative; the exclamative and biʾsa readings are intransitive, fixed, and performative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r6.anchor: وقد ظهرالفرق بين هذه الأوجه الثلاثة فإنها في الأول متعدية متصرفة والكلام معها خبر محض،

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r7.claim: The Shaykh distinguishes biʾsa from the exclamative by the rules on biʾsa’s subject and by its clause structure.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r7.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " والفرق بين هذا الوجه - يعني كونها بمعنى بئس - والوجه الذي قبله

SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r8.claim: The author says the Shaykh’s distinction needs interpretation: blame has a specific target that can form a subject-predicate construction, but this does not clearly distinguish the verbal clauses themselves.
SAMIN-DURR:6:31#4/r8.anchor: وظاهره لا يظهر إلا بتأويل وهو أن الذم لا بد فيه من مخصوص بالذم وهو مبتدأ

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r1.speaker: القفال وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal and others interpret meeting God as meeting the resurrection and its recompense, citing the threat against one who swears falsely to take a Muslim's property.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r1.anchor:
قيل: بالبعث بعد الموت وبالجزاء دليله قوله عليه السلام:
" من حلف على يمين كاذبة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r2.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r2.claim: Al-Qushayri rejects that interpretation: using meeting to mean recompense where context requires it does not justify doing so here; the phrase should retain its literal sense, since deniers of God and of vision deny existence.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r2.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لأن حمل اللقاء في موضع على الجزاء لدليل قائم لا يوجب هذا التأويل في كل موضع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r3.claim: The Hour is named for the rapid reckoning that occurs then; baghtatan means suddenly and is a circumstantial accusative, a verbal noun used as a state according to Sibawayh.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r3.anchor: سميت القيامة بالساعة لسرعة الحساب فيها. ومعنى «بغتة» فجأة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r4.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r4.claim: Sibawayh treats baghtatan as a verbal noun in the accusative of state, like qataltuhu sabran, but does not allow extending the pattern by analogy to saying someone came quickly.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r4.anchor: وهي عند سيبويه مصدر في موضع الحال، كما تقول: قتلته صبرا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r5.claim: Calling out to regret is not literal address: it intensifies sorrow, like calling on wonder; Sibawayh imagines summoning sorrow to arrive, stronger than simply saying one is amazed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r5.anchor: وقع النداء على الحسرة وليست بمنادى في الحقيقة، ولكنه يدل على كثرة التحسر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r6.claim: Another explanation treats the cry as a warning to people about the immense regret coming upon them, using an apparent addressee who is not literally being addressed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو تنبيه للناس على عظيم ما يحل بهم من الحسرة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r7.claim: Hasan says the neglected preparation was for the Hour itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r7.anchor: على ما فرطنا فيها } أي في الساعة، أي في التقدمة لها عن الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r8.claim: Farratna means we neglected or squandered; its root evokes going ahead, so the phrase may mean letting others precede us in obedience or failing to act for the Hour in worldly life.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.claim: Al-Tabari takes the pronoun to refer to a transaction: they regret trading faith for disbelief and the afterlife for worldly life, as the loss-of-trade wording in al-Baqara indicates.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.anchor: وقال الطبري: الهاء راجعة إلى الصفقة، وذلك أنهم لما تبين لهم خسران صفقتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r1.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says their regret concerns neglecting deeds that would lead to Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r1.anchor: وقال السدي: على ما ضيعنا أي من عمل الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r2.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri says the people of Hell see their homes in Paradise and cry out in regret.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r2.anchor: يرى أهل النار منازلهم في الجنة فيقولون: «يا حسرتنا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r3.claim: Their burdens are sins, described metaphorically as physical loads on their backs; wizr originates from the idea of a mountain or weight and also appears in the funeral phrase about returning burdened, not rewarded.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r3.anchor: أي ذنوبهم جمع وزر. { على ظهورهم } مجاز وتوسع وتشبيه بمن يحمل ثقلا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd says the funeral phrase should be mawzurat, burdened with sin, rather than the common ma'zurat, because the root is wizr.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r4.anchor: والعامة تقول: «مأزورات» كأنه لا وجه له عنده لأنه من الوزر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r5.claim: Wazir derives from carrying the burdens of governance; the verse means sins cling to the disbelievers and weigh them down, and the final clause calls their burden vile.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى أنهم لزمتهم الآثام فصاروا مثقلين بها

RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.claim: The verse portrays two losses for deniers of resurrection: they squandered bodily and intellectual faculties meant to gain enduring knowledge and virtue on transient pleasure, losing both their capital and supposed profit.
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.anchor: أعطاه العقل والتفكر أجل أن يتوصل باستعمال هذه الآلات والأدوات إلى تحصيل المعارف الحقيقية

RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.claim: This loss applies to deniers who believe present bodily pleasure is the highest happiness; believers expect resurrection and prepare provisions for the return, so they are not deceived by temporary goods.
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الخسران إنما يحصل لمن كان منكرا للبعث والقيامة

RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.claim: The other loss is that unbelievers prepare no provisions or detachment from worldly ties; after death they are strangers in the spiritual realm, grieving both their lack of preparation and separation from earthly pleasures.
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.anchor: فإذا مات بقي كالغريب في عالم الروحانيات ، وكالمنقطع عن أحبابه وأقاربه الذين كانوا في عالم الجسمانيات

RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.claim: Their lament about neglect points to failing to prepare for reward, while carrying loads on their backs points to having earned punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.anchor: فالأول : هو المراد من قوله { قالوا يأبانا * ياحسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها } والثاني : هو المراد من قوله { وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم }

RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r1.claim: Loss means forfeiting immense reward and receiving immense punishment; meeting God refers to denying resurrection, and the expression is apt because only God controls benefit, harm, elevation, and abasement at Judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r1.anchor: المراد منه الذين أنكروا البعث والقيامة

RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r2.claim: Until marks the endpoint of their denial, not of their loss, since loss has no endpoint: they persisted in denial until the sudden Hour made their regret appear.
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r2.anchor: كلمة ( حتى ) غاية لقوله { كذبوا } لا لقوله { قد خسر } لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له

RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r3.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that death is an entry into the states and preliminaries of the afterlife, so it is treated as part of the Hour; a prophetic saying states that whoever dies has had his Hour established.

RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r4.claim: The Hour is named either for the speed of reckoning or because it arrives suddenly at an unknown time; baghtatan can be a circumstantial adverb or an emphatic verbal noun.
RAZI-FULL:v12p163/r4.anchor: الساعة هي الوقت الذي تقوم القيامة سميت ساعة لأنها تفجأ الناس في ساعة لا يعلمها أحد

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says calling out يا حسرتنا alerts people to the regret awaiting them; Arabs intensify such events by addressing them directly, as in 36:30, 39:56, 11:72, and 12:84.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r1.anchor: أن النداء للحسرة ، والمراد منه تنبيه المخاطبين وهو قول الزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r2.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r2.claim: Sībawayhi takes regret itself as the addressee: the phrase means, in effect, O regret, come, for this is your time.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن المنادى هو نفس الحسرة على معنى : أن هذا وقتك فاحضري وهو قول سيبويه

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines farraṭtu fī al-shayʾ as neglecting or wasting it.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة يقال : فرطت في الشيء أي ضيعته

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives farraṭnā from advancing or letting something go ahead, so neglect is bringing failure forward.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : فرطنا أي قدمنا العجز جعله من قولهم فرط فلان إذا سبق وتقدم

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī summarizes al-Zajjāj’s account as neglect consisting in putting shortcoming first.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r5.anchor: قال الواحدي : فالتفريط عنده تقديم التقصير

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the pronoun in fīhā to refer to worldly life, though it was not explicitly mentioned; reason identifies it as the place of neglect.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس في الدنيا والسؤال عليه أنه لم يجر للدنيا ذكر

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the pronoun to refer to the Hour: they regret failing to prepare provisions for it.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r7.anchor: قال الحسن المراد يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا في الساعة

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r8.claim: Another view refers the pronoun to the implied deeds in ما فرطنا, namely the actions and acts of worship they neglected.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r8.anchor: أن تعود الكناية إلى معنى ما في قوله { ما فرطنا } أي حسرتنا على الأعمال والطاعات التي فرطنا فيها

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r9.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the pronoun refers to the transaction implied by خسِروا: their lament concerns the bargain they lost.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r9.anchor: قال محمد بن جرير الطبري : الكناية تعود إلى الصفقة لأنه تعالى لما ذكر الخسران

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r10.claim: Failing to prepare for reward and earning grounds for severe punishment together constitute the ultimate loss.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r10.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم لم يحصلوا لأنفسهم ما به يستحقون الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the loads as sins and errors; the root sense of a burden explains why sins are called weights.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الأوزار الآثام والخطايا قال أهل اللغة الوزر الثقل

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r12.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r12.claim: Abū ʿUbayda illustrates the root w-z-r with carrying goods in a garment, the burdens of war, and a ruler’s minister carrying the weight of delegated administration.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r12.anchor: يقال للرجل إذا بسط ثوبه فجعل فيه المتاع أحمل وزرك وأوزار الحرب أثقالها من السلاح

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r13.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that people carry the weight of their sins.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج : وهم يحملون أوزارهم أي يحملون ثقل ذنوبهم

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r14.speaker: قتادة والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r14.claim: A report attributed to Qatāda and al-Suddī says righteous or corrupt deeds meet their owners after resurrection as a beautiful pleasant-smelling or ugly foul-smelling mount, and each carries or is carried by that deed; 19:85 is cited.

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r15.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r15.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the weight metaphorically: the punishment of their sins is painful and burdensome.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r15.anchor: الثقل كما يذكر في المنقول ، فقد يذكر أيضا في الحال والصفة

RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r16.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r16.claim: Others say their sins remain inseparable from them, as in saying that someone’s memory stands constantly before one’s eyes.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164/r16.anchor: معنى قوله { وهم يحملون أوزارهم } أي لا تزايلهم أوزارهم

RAZI-FULL:v12p164#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p164#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p164#2/r1.claim: The closing phrase means how evil is what they bear; detailed treatment of the expression is deferred to the discussion of 4:22.
RAZI-FULL:v12p164#2/r1.anchor: { ألا ساء ما يزرون } والمعنى بئس الشيء الذي يزرونه أي يحملونه

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r1.claim: The Quran commonly calls those who disbelieve in life losers in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r1.anchor: The Quran commonly refers to those who disbelieved in this life as being lost or “losers” in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r2.claim: Those who deny meeting God and suppose worldly life is all will suddenly recognize their error at the Hour, the Resurrection and universal judgment.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r2.anchor: thinking there is naught but our life in this world (v. 29), will have the realization of their error “come upon them suddenly”

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r3.claim: Their cry expresses regret that they failed to prepare for the coming day.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r3.anchor: Their cry, Alas for us, expresses their regret over failing to prepare for this day

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī explains their regret as existential anguish at wasting God-given intellect and faculties meant to disclose truth and cultivate virtue.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r4.anchor: a deep, existential regret, as disbelievers realize that they have squandered the intellect and other faculties bestowed upon them by God

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r5.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī compares their loss to an investment that earns no return and loses the borrowed principal as well.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r5.anchor: lose not only the anticipated return on an investment, but the borrowed principal as well

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r6.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r6.claim: The burdens on their backs may be their own sins and transgressions.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r6.anchor: may be their sins and transgressions themselves

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r7.claim: Another interpretation identifies the burden as God’s wrath earned by sin.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r7.anchor: or the burden of wrath from God that is earned as a result of those sins

STUDYQURAN:6:31/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r8.claim: A further interpretation is the burden of warnings and reminders they ignored; 20:100–101 says the reminder becomes a Hereafter burden.
STUDYQURAN:6:31/r8.anchor: or the burden of the warning and reminders they refused to heed in their earthly lives

TAB-FULL:v9p214/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r1.claim: He identifies the deniers as people who reject resurrection, judgment, Paradise, and Hell, including Quraysh polytheists and their followers.
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r1.anchor: بالكفر {الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله} [الأنعام: 31] يعني: الذين أنكروا البعث بعد الممات والثواب والعقاب

TAB-FULL:v9p214/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r2.claim: The definite Hour means the known Hour when God raises the dead from their graves.
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r2.anchor: {حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة} [الأنعام: 31] يقول: حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة التي يبعث الله فيها الموتى من قبورهم

TAB-FULL:v9p214/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r3.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly, without the person being surprised knowing when the event will happen.
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r3.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {بغتة} [الأنعام: 31] فجأة من غير علم من تفجؤه بوقت مفاجأتها إياه

TAB-FULL:v9p214/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r4.claim: Their cry is regret for ruining the transaction in which they exchanged faith and their share of Paradise for disbelief and punishment.
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r4.anchor: يا ندامتنا على ما ضيعنا فيها يعني في صفقتهم تلك

TAB-FULL:v9p214/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r5.claim: The feminine pronoun in فيها refers to the transaction, omitted because the mention of loss already implies a failed sale.
TAB-FULL:v9p214/r5.anchor: والهاء والألف في قوله: {فيها} [البقرة: 25] من ذكر الصفقة، ولكن اكتفى بدلالة قوله

TAB-FULL:v9p215/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p215/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p215/r1.claim: He explains their regret as sorrow for wasting the deeds that would have earned Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v9p215/r1.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا} [الأنعام: 31] فيها أما {يا حسرتنا} [الأنعام: 31] : «فندامتنا على ما فرطنا فيها

TAB-FULL:v9p215/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p215/r2.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v9p215/r2.claim: The Prophet says people of Hell will see their places in Paradise and cry in regret.
TAB-FULL:v9p215/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، في قوله: {يا حسرتنا} [الأنعام: 31] قال: " يرى أهل النار منازلهم من الجنة

TAB-FULL:v9p217/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r1.claim: He explains the root of wizr as sinning: the Arabs say a people committed sin and are burdened by it.
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r1.anchor: أثم، فإن أريد أنهم أثموا قيل: قد وزر القوم فهم يوزرون وهم موزورون

TAB-FULL:v9p217/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r2.claim: He rejects glossing wizr as a physical burden, lacking either a known attestation or a trustworthy report from Arabs.
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r2.anchor: وقد زعم بعضهم أن الوزر: الثقل والحمل. ولست أعرف ذلك كذلك في شاهد ولا من رواية ثقة عن العرب

TAB-FULL:v9p217/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r3.claim: The phrase says on their backs to specify where they carry the sins, since burdens can be carried on the head, shoulder, or elsewhere.
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r3.anchor: وقال تعالى ذكره: {على ظهورهم} [الأنعام: 31] لأن الحمل قد يكون على الرأس والمنكب وغير ذلك

TAB-FULL:v9p217/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r4.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الملائي
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r4.claim: He describes a person's good or evil deeds meeting him after burial in fitting forms and riding him on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r4.anchor: ثنا عمرو بن قيس الملائي، قال: " إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله عمله في أحسن صورة

TAB-FULL:v9p217/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r5.claim: He depicts a sinner's ugly, foul-smelling deed as accompanying him in the grave and riding his back to drive him into Hell.
TAB-FULL:v9p217/r5.anchor: عن السدي: {وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم} [الأنعام: 31] قال: " ليس من رجل ظالم يموت فيدخل قبره

TAB-FULL:v9p217#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p217#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p217#2/r1.claim: He paraphrases the closing condemnation as saying how evil their deeds are.
TAB-FULL:v9p217#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {ألا ساء ما يزرون} [الأنعام: 31] قال: «ساء ما يعملون»

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r1.claim: بغتة means suddenly; بغته الأمر is used when something comes upon a person without warning.
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r1.anchor:
كل ما جاء فجاءة فقد بغت، يقال قد بغته الأمر يبغته بغتا وبغتة، إذا أتاه
فجاءة.

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses بغتة for an unforeseen death, illustrating suddenness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r2.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
ولكنهم ماتوا ولم أخش بغتة. . . وأفظع شيء حين يفجؤك البغت

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r3.claim: Calling out to حسرة intensifies news of a terrible event: Arabs use a vocative form to draw listeners’ attention, though grief itself cannot understand or answer.
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r3.anchor:
فالجواب عن ذلك أن العرب إذا اجتهدت في الإخبار عن عظيم تقع فيه
جعلته نداء، فلفظه لفظ ما ينبه، والمنبه غيره.

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh explains يا عجباه as calling wonder to come, and يا حسرتاه as alerting people that they have lost; the apparent addressee is really the audience.
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r4.anchor:
قال سيبويه: " إنك إذا قلت يا عجباه، فكأنك قلت احضر وتعال يا
عجب فإنه من أزمانك،

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r5.claim: The same idiom appears in لا أرينك ههنا: although phrased as the speaker’s own action, it means the addressee must stay away because otherwise the speaker will see him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r5.anchor: قولك: لا أرينك ههنا، فلفظك لفظ الناهي نفسه

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r6.claim: يا حسرتنا therefore alerts the audience rather than addressing a non-rational abstraction.
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r6.anchor: قد علم أن الحسرة لا تدعى، فوقع التنبيه للمخاطبين.

ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p240#2/r7.claim: فرطنا فيها means that they had previously fallen short through incapacity or neglect.

ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r1.claim: Carrying their burdens means carrying the weight of their sins; punishment is compared to a heavy load, and Arabic also uses ‘heavy’ for severe dislike.
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r1.anchor:
أي يحملون ثقل ذنوبهم، وهذا مثل. جائز أن يكون جعل ما ينالهم
من العذاب بمنزلة أثقل ما يحمل،

ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r2.claim: وزر is connected with a mountain refuge on which a ruler or prophet relies for aid; the same root appears in calling Aaron a minister.
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r2.anchor: واشتقاقه من الوزر، وهو الجبل الذي يعتصم به الملك والنبي، أي يعينه.

ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r3.claim: ساء ما يزرون means ‘evil is what they carry’; the clause follows the syntax of نعم and بئس, as in ‘ساء مثلا القوم.’
ZAJJAJ:v2p242/r3.anchor:
أي بئس الشيء شيئا أي يحملونه، وقد فسرنا عمل نعم وبئس فيما
مضى من الكتاب، وكذلك (ساء مثلا القوم)

TABATABAI:6:21-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r1.claim: The cosmos assigns each goal a proper route; bypassing that route disables its cause and damages connected causes, as trying to sustain life without eating and digestion would disable nourishment and growth.
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r1.anchor: فلكل غاية مطلوبة وسعادة مقصودة طريق خاص لا يسلك إليها إلا منه

TABATABAI:6:21-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r2.claim: Human beliefs about God and the afterlife and practical laws are paths to human happiness; injustice cannot secure lasting happiness because the wider order opposes it and eventually ruins its apparent gains.
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r2.anchor: وهذه طرق إلى السعادات الإنسانية بحسب طبعها لا طريق إليها دونها

TABATABAI:6:21-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r3.claim: Wrongdoing can include shirk, seizing property, violating honor or life, neglecting worship, and related lies or deception; a person may seem pleased with a gain while losing in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:6:21-32/r3.anchor: فالظالم ربما دعته طاغية الشره إلى أن يستعمل ما له من العزة بالإثم والقدرة الكاذبة

TABATABAI:6:28-31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:28-31/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:28-31/r6.claim: The sequence uses resurrection, gathering, and the Hereafter, then calls it meeting God; this wording links the Hour with that encounter.
TABATABAI:6:28-31/r6.anchor: حيث بدل الحشر والبعث والقيامة المذكورات في سابق الكلام لقاء ثم ذكر الساعة

TABATABAI:6:30-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains baghtatan as anything that comes suddenly or unexpectedly.
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r2.anchor: قال في المجمع كل شيء أتى فجأه فقد بغت

TABATABAI:6:30-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib explains hasrah as grief and regret for what was lost, deriving it from uncovering or from depleted strength and exhaustion.
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r3.anchor: والحسرة الغم على ما فاته والندم عليه كأنه انحسر عنه الجهل

TABATABAI:6:30-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib gives wizr the sense of a mountain refuge and, by analogy with a mountain's weight, a burden or sin; the Qur'an also uses it for burdens carried.
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r4.anchor: وقال الوزر بفتحتين الملجأ الذي يتلجأ إليه من الجبل

TABATABAI:6:30-32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r5.claim: The sudden Hour brings regret for neglect and makes sins appear as burdens carried on backs, the gravest human condition; the burden may mean weight, sin, or sin's consequence.
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r5.anchor: والآية تبين تبعة أخرى من تبعات إنكارهم البعث وهو أن الساعة سيفاجئهم فينادون بالحسرة على تفريطهم فيها

TABATABAI:6:30-32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:30-32/r6.claim: The verse is the conclusion of their claim that earthly life is all there is: by trading the afterlife and meeting God for denial, they have lost their bargain.

TABATABAI:6:31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:31/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:6:31/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ transmits from al-Aʿmash through Abu Salih that the people of Hell see their places in Paradise and cry out in regret.
TABATABAI:6:31/r2.anchor: وفي المجمع عن الأعمش عن أبي صالح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABRISI:6:31-32/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32/r3.claim: Baght means sudden arrival; ḥasra is intense regret that exhausts the regretful; tafrīṭ means falling short, originally putting forward, while afrāṭ is excess and tafrīṭ is delay or shortcoming.
TABRISI:6:31-32/r3.anchor: والحسرة شدة الندم حتى يحسر النادم كما يحسر الذي تقوم به دابته في السفر البعيد

TABRISI:6:31-32/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32/r4.claim: Wizr means a burden and is etymologically linked to a cord of reliance; wazīr is likened to someone on whom a ruler relies.
TABRISI:6:31-32/r4.anchor: والوزر الثقل في اللغة واشتقاقه من الوزر وهو الحبل الذي يعتصم به

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r1.claim: Yazirūn is a verb from wizr, “to sin”; mawzūr describes one burdened by wrongdoing, while common speech substitutes maʾzūr. The related Qurʾānic use of wazīr is cited.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r1.anchor: ويزرون يفعلون من وزر يزر وزرا إذا أثم. وقيل: وزر فهو موزور إذا فعل به ذلك

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r2.claim: ʿAql, nahy, and ḥijā share the sense of restraint: reason restrains wrongdoing and the self; nahy implies holding back, while ḥijā is from remaining or holding fast.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r2.anchor: والعقل والنهي والحجي متقاربة المعنى فالعقل الإمساك عن القبيح وقصر النفس وحبسها

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī explains that a place called Maʿqala holds water, just as medicine restrains the belly, illustrating the restraining sense of ʿaql.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r3.anchor: الأصمعي: وبالدهناء خبراء يقال له معقلة قال وتراها سميت معقلة

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r4.claim: Nahy can be a verbal noun or a plural and conveys holding and restraint; its related terms name the low place where water stops and collects.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r4.anchor: والنهى لا يخلو أن يكون مصدرا كالهدى أو جمعا كالظلم وهو في معنى ثبات وحبس

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r5.claim: Ḥijā comes from ḥajw, lingering or holding back; a cited verse witnesses ḥajā, and al-Azharī says taḥajjaytu means I held fast, with or without hamza.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r5.anchor: الحجى أصله من الحجو وهو احتباس وتمكث

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r6.claim: The phrase “until the Hour comes” marks the endpoint of their denial; the governing verb is “they denied,” and the sudden Hour brings regret too late to help.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r6.anchor: معناها منتهى تكذيبهم الحسرة يوم القيامة والعامل فيها كذبوا

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r7.claim: Calling to regret is an emphatic Arabic device: a grave matter is cast as a vocative, summoning regret to appear. Al-Zajjāj and Sībawayh explain it as an attention-getting call whose real addressee is the audience.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r7.anchor: إن العرب إذا اجتهدت في المبالغة في الإخبار عن أمر عظيم تقع فيه جعلته نداء فلفظه لفظ ما ينبه

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r8.claim: “How bad is what they bear” is parsed as “evil is the burden they carry,” applying the previously discussed syntax of niʿma and biʾsa.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r8.anchor: وقوله ساءنا يزرون تقديره بئس الشيء يزرونه

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan take meeting God as meeting what God promised of reward and punishment, figuratively attributing the meeting of recompense to God.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r9.anchor: يعني بلقاء ما وعد الله به من الثواب والعقاب وجعل لقائهم لذلك لقاء له تعالى مجازا عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r10.claim: Another explanation takes “meeting God” as meeting His recompense, as in saying a dead person has met the reward of his deed.
TABRISI:6:31-32#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد بلقاء جزاء الله كما يقال للميت لقي فلان عمله أي لقي جزاء عمله

TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r1.claim: Meeting God means meeting what God promised of reward and punishment; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan call this a figurative attribution of meeting the recompense to meeting God.
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r1.anchor: إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه

TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r2.claim: Another explanation takes “meeting God” as meeting the recompense of God, as in saying that a dead person has met his deed’s reward.
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r2.anchor: أي القيامة { بغتة } أي فجأة من غير أن يعلموا وقتها

TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r3.claim: The regret is for failing in worldly life to prepare deeds for the Hereafter, according to Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r3.anchor: أي على ما تركنا وضيعنا في الدنيا من تقديم أعمال الآخرة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the pronoun in “fīhā” to refer to the Hour: they regret neglecting work and preparation for it.
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن الهاء يعود إلى الساعة عن الحسن

TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r5.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r5.claim: Al-Suddī takes the pronoun to refer to Paradise: they regret failing to seek and work for it. A report from the Prophet says the people of Hell see their places in Paradise and lament.
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r5.anchor: إن الهاء يعود إلى الجنة أي في طلبها والعمل لها عن السدي يدل عليه ما رواه الأعمش

TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
