TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r6.speaker: محمد بن جرير
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r6.claim: Muḥammad b. Jarīr says the pronoun refers to the transaction, inferred from the mention of loss; alternatively, it refers to the good deeds neglected, with mā relative rather than a verbal noun.
TABRISI:6:31-32#3/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن جرير: الهاء يعود إلى الصفقة لأنه لما ذكر الخسران

TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r1.claim: Carrying burdens on their backs means bearing the weight of their sins and offenses, according to Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد آثامهم وخطاياهم

TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r2.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī describe deeds as embodied companions: good deeds carry believers after resurrection, while evil deeds ride and burden disbelievers.
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أحسن شيء صورة

TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads the carrying as a permissible metaphor: punishment for sins weighs on them like a heavy load, since weight can describe distress as well as physical mass.
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هذا مثل جائز أن يكون جعل ما ينالهم من العذاب

TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r4.claim: “Evil is what they bear” either condemns the burden itself, as Ibn ʿAbbās says, or the punishment they suffer as recompense for their evil deeds.
TABRISI:6:31-32#4/r4.anchor: أي بئس الحمل حملهم عن ابن عباس. وقيل: معناه ساء ما ينالهم جزاء لذنوبهم

THALABI:v4p144/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v4p144/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd explains wazr as a load carried in a cloak and connects the minister, wazīr, with supporting or sheltering a king or prophet; Moses' prayer is cited.
THALABI:v4p144/r1.anchor: واشتقاقه من الوزر الذي يعتصم به

THALABI:v4p144/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144/r2.speaker: السدي وعمرو بن قيس الملائي
THALABI:v4p144/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and Amr ibn Qays describe a believer's righteous deeds appearing after burial as a beautiful, fragrant figure who lets the believer ride them on the Resurrection journey.
THALABI:v4p144/r2.anchor: أنا عملك الصالح طال ما ركبتك في الدنيا فاركبني اليوم أنت

THALABI:v4p144/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144/r3.speaker: السدي وعمرو بن قيس الملائي
THALABI:v4p144/r3.claim: In the same report, an unbeliever's evil deeds appear as an ugly, foul figure and say that the person who rode them in life must now be ridden by them.
THALABI:v4p144/r3.anchor: أنا عملك السيء طالما ركبتني في المساء فأنا أركبك اليوم

THALABI:v4p144/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144/r4.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v4p144/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses carrying burdens on backs as carrying and doing them, and says evil is what they carry.
THALABI:v4p144/r4.anchor: ألا ساء ما يزرون أي يحملون ويعملون

THALABI:v4p144#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144#2/r1.speaker: أبو يزيد المدني
THALABI:v4p144#2/r1.claim: Abu Jahl acknowledged Muhammad’s truth after a handshake, but said he could not follow a man from Banu Abd Manaf; the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v4p144#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد المدني: لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا جهل فصافحه

THALABI:v4p144#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144#2/r2.speaker: ناجية بن كعب
THALABI:v4p144#2/r2.claim: Najiya reports Abu Jahl saying he did not accuse Muhammad of lying, but rejected the message he brought; the verse followed.
THALABI:v4p144#2/r2.anchor: وقال ناجية بن كعب: قال أبو جهل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما نتهمك ولا نكذبك

THALABI:v4p144#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p144#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v4p144#2/r3.claim: Maqatil identifies al-Harith ibn Amir: he privately believed Muhammad truthful but feared Arab retaliation and loss of security if he followed him.
THALABI:v4p144#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف بن قصي

ASAD-NOTES:6:31#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:31#n21/r1.speaker: Ibn ‘Abbas
ASAD-NOTES:6:31#n21/r1.claim: Ibn ‘Abbas interprets the carried burdens as the sinners’ burdens of sin; Asad adopts this interpretation through Razi.
ASAD-NOTES:6:31#n21/r1.anchor: interpretation given by Ibn 'Abbas, as quoted by Razi

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r1.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r1.claim: They are losers because they traded faith for disbelief, destroying their own souls in punishment; the gravest work-loss is a ruined soul, as commerce’s worst loss is its capital.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r1.anchor: باعوا الإيمان بالكفر، فعظم خسرانهم في ذلك البيع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r2.claim: Meeting God means resurrection, reward, punishment, and return to Him; the author links this explanation to 2:46.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r2.anchor: يريد بالبعث والثواب والعقاب والمصير إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r3.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r3.claim: The phrase means meeting God’s recompense; “meeting God” names meeting one’s deeds’ recompense, as people say a dead person met his deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p82/r3.anchor: المعنى هاهنا كذبوا # بلقاء جزاء الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r1.claim: Ḥattā marks the endpoint of their denial: they denied until the Resurrection appeared suddenly and regret began.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r1.anchor: {حتى} هاهنا بيان أن منتهى تكذيبهم الحسرة يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r2.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r2.claim: The Hour is the Day of Resurrection, so called because reckoning and recompense are completed with extraordinary speed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r2.anchor: يوم القيامة الساعة؛ لسرعة الحساب للجزاء فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r3.claim: The Hour is the time when Resurrection begins, named for its sudden onset; this better fits baghtatan, which means suddenly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r3.anchor: وهذا القول أصح. ألا ترى أنه قال: {بغتة} والبغت والبغتة (¬3): الفجأة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r4.claim: No one knows when the Hour will come except God, so it catches people unawares.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p83/r4.anchor: يريد أن الساعة لا يعلمها أحد إلا هو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r1.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r1.claim: Calling out “our regret” alerts hearers to a terrible calamity and is more emphatic than simply saying regret is upon us; Arabic figurative address can target someone other than the literal addressee.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r1.anchor: معنى دعاء الحسرة: تنبيه الناس على ما وقع بهم من الحسرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r2.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r2.claim: The vocative summons regret as if telling it to come: this is your time; thus “our regret” means attend to our loss.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p84/r2.anchor: تأويل يا حسرتاه: انتبهوا على أنا قد خسرنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد، وأبو عبيدة، وأكثر أهل اللغة، والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r1.claim: Farraṭnā means we neglected or wasted; the regret concerns abandoned work for the Afterlife.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r2.claim: Farraṭnā means we put incapacity first, construing neglect as bringing shortcoming forward.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r3.claim: The pronoun in fīhā refers to worldly life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r4.claim: The pronoun refers to the Hour: they neglected the work and preparation needed for it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r4.anchor: روي عن الحسن أنه قال: (في الساعة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r5.claim: The pronoun refers to Paradise, meaning they neglected seeking it and working for it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r6.claim: The pronoun may refer to the implied deeds themselves: regret over good works and acts of obedience that they neglected.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن تعود الكناية إلى معنى {ما}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r7.claim: The pronoun may refer to the implied transaction: the preceding mention of loss signals the sale.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p86/r7.anchor: الكناية تعود إلى الصفقة؛ لأنه لما ذكر الخسران دل على الصفقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r1.claim: Awzār are the heavy burden of sin: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses them as sins and errors, while al-Zajjāj says they carry the weight of their sins.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r2.claim: Wizr originally means a load one carries, explaining both sins as burdens and the phrase “no bearer bears”; the root also appears in ordinary loading and in “minister.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r3.speaker: المفسرون؛ قتادة؛ السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r3.claim: Good and evil deeds appear as riders after resurrection: the believer rides beautiful, fragrant good work, while the unbeliever is ridden by foul, ugly evil work; this explains the image of bearing sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r3.anchor: إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أحسن شيء سورة وأطيبه ريحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r4.claim: Bearing sins can figuratively describe enduring punishment as a crushing weight, since heaviness describes emotional states as well as physical loads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r4.anchor: هذا مثل جائز أن يكون جعل ما ينالهم من العذاب بمنزلة أثقل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r5.speaker: أهل العربية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r5.claim: The image may mean sins never leave them, like saying someone’s person is before one’s eyes to mean the person remains constantly in mind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p88/r5.anchor: لا تزايلهم أوزارهم، كما تقول: شخصك نصب عيني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p91/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p91/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p91/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the load as an evil burden; al-Zajjāj says what they carry is a bad thing, with the wording discussed at 4:22.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r4.claim: Those denying the meeting with God lose when the Hour suddenly arrives; they lament neglecting the work of the Hereafter during worldly life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r4.anchor: قصرنا وضيعنا عمل الآخرة في الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r5.claim: Their sins are burdens on their backs; on leaving the grave, their evil deed appears foul and reeking and says it will now ride them as they rode it in life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:29-31/r5.anchor: استقبله عمله أقبح شيء صورة، وأخبثه ريحا،

ELMALILI:6:26-32/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r10.claim: Those who deny meeting God remain in loss until the Hour overtakes them suddenly; they lament their neglect while bearing their burdens on their backs, a terrible load.
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r10.anchor: Tâ vakt ü sâat kendilerine ansızın gelinceye kadar inkâr ettiler de o vakit

ELMALILI:6:26-32/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r11.claim: The deniers of resurrection and the Judgment have two further states: loss and the carrying of great burdens and sins.
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r11.anchor: Bu âyette ba‘s ü kıyameti inkâr edenlerin diğer bir hâlleri îzah olunmuştur ki birisi hüsran, birisi de büyük vizirler, veballer çekmektir.

ELMALILI:6:26-32/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r12.claim: Khusran is losing sight of immense reward and lasting bliss; vizr or wabal means being caught within immense punishment.
ELMALILI:6:26-32/r12.anchor: “Hüsran” sevâb-ı azîmin, na‘îm-i mukīmin fevt ü zayâ‘ını görmek, “vizr” ü “vebal” de ikāb-ı azîmin içinde kalmaktır.

ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r1.claim: Saʿa ordinarily means a small unit of time, one twenty-fourth of day and night; with the article it names the Day of Judgment and accountability, possibly because its accounting is swift.
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r1.anchor: “Sâ‘at”, eczâ-yı zamandan bir cüz’-i kalîlin ismidir ki gece ile gündüzün yirmi dört cüz’de bir cüz’üdür.

ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r2.claim: A second view takes al-Saʿa to mean the moment the Resurrection begins, named for its sudden arrival at an hour known only to God.
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r2.anchor: İkinci bir kavle göre de kıyâmetin koptuğu vaktin ismidir ki Allah’tan başka kimsenin bilmediği bir saatte ansızın bastıracağından dolayı tesmiye edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r3.claim: Death is also called a kind of resurrection because it begins the transition to the Hereafter.
ELMALILI:6:26-32#2/r3.anchor: vakt-i mevt de âhirete intikalin bir başlangıcı ve mukaddimesi olmak itibariyle mevt de kıyamet cinsinden addedilip o nâm ile yâd olunmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r1.claim: Exegetes say past-tense verbs describe resurrection and afterlife events as if already occurred, stressing their certainty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r1.anchor: Müfessirler, bu ifadelerde, ba‘s ve âhiret olaylarının sanki vuku bulmuş kadar kesin olduğunu vurgulamak için geçmiş zaman fiillerinin kullanıldığını belirtirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verses may describe what happens to each unbeliever after death: the soul sees the next life, recognizes its worldly disbelief as error, and admits it before God; this happens to those already dead and will happen to future dead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r2.anchor: ölen her insan gibi müşriklerin ruhları da bedenlerinden ayrıldıktan sonra ölümün ardından ikinci bir hayat daha olduğunu apaçık görmüş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r3.claim: Those denying that they will be brought before God are losers; when death or resurrection suddenly comes, they lament their failures while carrying their sins on their backs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:30/r3.anchor: İnsanlardan Allah’ın huzuruna çıkarılacaklarına inanmayanlar, bunu yalanlayanlar hüsrana uğramışlardır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p24/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p24/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p24/.claim: The passage contrasts the fate of Qur’an rejecters with that of people who denied the hereafter, whose loss becomes clear when the Hour suddenly arrives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p24/.anchor: these verses depict the fate of the rejecters of the hereafter.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#3/r1.speaker: author
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#3/r1.claim: The author glosses ‘evil is what they carry’ as ‘evil is what they do.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#3/r1.anchor: في قوله تعالى ﴿ ساء ما يزرون ﴾ قال ساء ما يعملون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r15.claim: البغتة means an unforeseen sudden arrival, coming quickly without awareness of its timing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r15.anchor: البغت والبغتة: الفجأة يقال بغته يبغته أي فجأه يفجأه وهي مجيء الشيء سرعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r16.claim: فرط means to fall short despite being able to avoid negligence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r16.anchor: فرط قصر مع القدرة على ترك التقصير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r17.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r17.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses فرط as wasting or neglecting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r17.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: فرط ضيع. وقال ابن بحر: فرط سبق والفارط السابق، وفرط خلى السبق لغيره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r18.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r18.claim: Ibn Bahr relates فرط to going ahead: the forerunner leaves the lead for another or lets it pass.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r18.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: فرط سبق والفارط السابق، وفرط خلى السبق لغيره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r19.claim: الأوزار means sins and errors; its root sense is a heavy load, as in the burdens of war and the minister’s burdens of rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r19.anchor: الأوزار: الآثام والخطايا وأصله الثقل من الحمل، وزرته جملته وأوزار الحرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r20.claim: The word الوزير is connected to bearing the burdens assigned by the ruler.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p451/r20.anchor: ومنه الوزير لأنه يحمل عن السلطان أثقال ما يسند إليه من تدبير ملكه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r5.claim: God reports the loss of those who denied resurrection: they exchanged saving faith for disbelief that brings ruin, like a failed bargain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r5.anchor: هذا استئناف إخبار من الله تعالى عن أحوال منكري البعث وخسرانهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r6.claim: لقاء الله means reaching the afterlife and its judgment; another explanation takes it as meeting His recompense, with the possessive construction magnifying it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى بلقاء الله بلوغ الآخرة وما يكون فيها من الجزاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r7.claim: حتى marks the limit of their denial, not of their loss, since loss continues; the author refers to an earlier discussion of حتى إذا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p480#2/r7.anchor: وحتى غاية لتكذيبهم لا لخسرانهم، لأن الخسران لا غاية له والتكذيب مغيا بالحسرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says they lament at death because death begins the states of the afterlife, so it is treated as the Hour; its onset is swift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r1.anchor: لما كان الموت وقوعا في أحوال الآخرة ومقدماتها، جعل من جنس الساعة وسمي باسمها ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r2.claim: The author says the Hour can mean the actual Resurrection, when they also lament; their simultaneous burden-bearing fits that reading better than a future state at death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r2.anchor: ويمكن حمل الساعة على الحقيقة وهو يوم القيامة ولا يلزم من تحسرهم وقت الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r3.claim: The dead perceive their time in the barzakh as only a day, so denial ends when the Resurrection makes the messengers’ warning visible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r3.anchor: إذ مكثهم في البرزخ على اعتقاد أمثلهم طريقة يوم واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r5.claim: بغتة may be an adverbial circumstance of the Hour, of those overtaken, a verbal noun for جاء, or from an omitted verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r5.anchor: وجوزوا في انتصاب بغتة أن يكون مصدرا في موضع الحال من الساعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r6.claim: Sibawayh says calling abstract sorrow summons it to appear, magnifying the moment for speaker and hearer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه: وكأن الذي ينادي الحسرة أو العجب أو السرور أو الويل يقول: اقربي أو احضري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r7.claim: فرطنا means we fell short despite being able to avoid it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r7.anchor: وفرطنا قصرنا والتفريط التقصير مع القدرة على تركه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r8.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r8.claim: Al-Hasan takes فيها to refer to the Hour: they neglected to prepare for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r8.anchor: فيها عائد على الساعة أي في التقدمة لها قاله الحسن، أو الصفقة التي تضمنها ذكر الخسارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r9.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r9.claim: Al-Tabari takes فيها as referring to the failed transaction implied by loss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r9.anchor: أو الصفقة التي تضمنها ذكر الخسارة قاله الطبري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says فيها refers to worldly life, understood despite not being named, or to the Hour and its preparation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الضمير للحياة الدنيا جيء بضميرها وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لكونها معلومة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas also takes the pronoun as referring to worldly life; reason indicates that this is where they fell short.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r11.anchor: وكونه عائدا على الدنيا وهو قول ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r12.claim: Another possibility makes ما a relative pronoun: they lament the deeds and acts of obedience they neglected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p481/r12.anchor: وقيل: يعود الضمير على ما وهي اسم موصول وعاد على لمعنى أي يا حسرتنا على الأعمال والطاعات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the burdens as sins and transgressions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r1.anchor: الأوزار الخطايا والآثام قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r2.speaker: عمير بن هانئ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r2.claim: Umayr ibn Hani, Amr ibn Qays al-Mula’i, al-Suddi, and al-Tabari take the load literally: deeds appear as an ugly, foul-smelling man who rides the sinner to Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا الحمل حقيقة وهو قول عمير بن هانئ وعمرو بن قيس الملائي والسدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits from the Prophet a report with the same meaning, though its wording differs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r3.anchor: ورواه أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذا المعنى واللفظ مختلف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r4.claim: A figurative reading takes carrying the burden to mean enduring the pain and hardship caused by sins; Ibn Atiyya presents it first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو مجاز عبر بحل الوزر عن ما يجده من المشقة والآلام بسبب ذنوبه، والمعنى أنهم يقاسون عقاب ذنوبهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives only the figurative reading, comparing it with hands as the familiar means of earning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r5.anchor: وهذا القول بدأ به ابن عطية ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r6.claim: The circumstantial waw introduces their burden-bearing; the explicit pronoun repeats the subject for stronger attribution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r6.anchor: والواو في وهم واو الحال وأتت الجملة مصدرة بالضمير لأنه أبلغ في النسبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r7.claim: The back is the customary place for burdens and emphasizes weight because it bears more than the head or shoulder.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r7.anchor: وخص الظهر لأنه غالبا موضع اعتياد الحمل ولأنه يشعر بالمبالغة في ثقل المحمول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r9.claim: ساء ما يزرون has three analyses: ordinary transitive “it grieves them,” an exclamatory “how evil,” or emphatic blame like بئس.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p483/r9.anchor: ساء هنا تحتمل وجوها ثلاثة. أحدها: أن تكون المتعدية المتصرفة ووزنها فعل بفتح العين والمعنى ألا ساءهم ما يزرون

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.claim: The losers are the previously described disbelievers; the relative clause replaces a pronoun to show their loss results from denying and persisting in denial of meeting God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.anchor: هم الكفار الذين حكيت أحوالهم لكن وضع الموصول موضع الضمير للايذان بتسبب خسرانهم عما في حيز الصلة من التكذيب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r2.claim: Al-Alusi reports that meeting God means meeting what He promised, citing Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan; other exegetes supply reward or take the phrase as a representation of resurrection and its sequel.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r2.anchor: والمراد به لقاء ما وعد سبحانه وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r3.claim: Some exegetes make the implicit complement 'meeting God's reward'; others read meeting God as a representative metaphor for resurrection and what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r3.anchor: وصرح بعضهم بتقدير المضاف أي لقاء جزاء بالله تعالى وصرح آخرون بأن لقاء الله تعالى استعارة تمثيلية عن البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r4.claim: The Hour is the appointed Judgment Day; saʿah originally means a short stretch of time and became the name of the known time, either because it is brief beside eternity or its reckoning is swift.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r4.anchor: وأصل الساعة القطعة من الزمان وغلبت على الوقت المعلوم كالنجم للثريا وسمي ساعة لقلته بالنسبة لما بعده من الخلود

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r5.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r5.claim: Some interpret the Hour here as the time of death.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r6.claim: The 'until' may mark the end of their denial, or the end of loss in its ordinary sense: like Satan's curse lasting until Judgment, they then meet a calamity that eclipses earlier losses.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r6.anchor: غاية الخسران لكن بالمعنى المتعارف والكلام حينئذ على حد قوله تعالى : وان عليك لعنتيلعنتي إلى يوم الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r7.claim: Baghtah means suddenly, without awareness; it can be a circumstantial verbal noun of the subject or object, or a cognate accusative of the verb or an implied verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r7.anchor: أي فجأو وبغتة بالتحريك مثلها وبغتة كمنعة فجأة أي هجم عليه من غير شعور

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r8.claim: They answer the conditional with 'O our remorse'; this personifies remorse and summons it as though it could arrive at its appointed moment.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r8.anchor: نداء للحسرة وهي شدة الندم كأنه قيل : يا حسرتنا تعالى فهذا أوانك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies 'be present, O remorse'; this figurative summons alerts them to the causes of regret, since remorse itself cannot literally be called or arrive.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : التقدير يا حسرة احضري هذا أو انك وهو نداء مجازي ومعناه تنبيه أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p131#2/r10.claim: The cited prophetic saying that whoever dies has had his resurrection occur explains why death may be treated as the beginning of the Hour.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r1.claim: Tafrit means neglecting what one was able to do; Abu Ubayda glosses it as waste, while Ibn Bahr derives it from going ahead and leaving precedence to another.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r1.anchor: فالتفريط التقصير فيما قدر على فعله وقال أبو عبيدة معناه التضييع وقال ابن بحر : معناه السبق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r2.claim: On Ibn Bahr's derivation, the doubled consonant conveys removal, as in scraping and stripping the camel's hide.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r2.anchor: فالتضعيف فيه للسلب كجلدت البعير أرلت جلده وسلبته

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r3.claim: The pronoun in 'therein' may refer to worldly life, according to Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r3.anchor: أي الحياة الدنيا كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r4.claim: Al-Hasan takes 'therein' to refer to the Hour, meaning failure to prepare for it through faith and good deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r4.anchor: أو في الساعة كما روي عن الحسن والمراد من التفريط في الساعة التقصير في مراعاة حقها والاستعداد لها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r5.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the pronoun refers to Paradise, meaning that they failed to seek it; al-Alusi considers this reading remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r5.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للجنة أي على ما فرطنا في طلبها ونسب إلى السدي ولا يخفى بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r6.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r6.claim: Al-Tabarsi cites a report from the Prophet, through al-Aʿmash, Abu Salih and Abu Saʿid, that the Fire's inhabitants see their places in Paradise and lament; al-Alusi says this cannot settle the interpretation while other possibilities remain.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r6.anchor: ما رواه الأعمش عن أبي صالح عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في هذه الآية : يرى أهل النار منازلهم من الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r7.speaker: محمد بن جرير
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Jarir says the pronoun returns to the quality implied by 'loss'; al-Alusi also regards this as remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r7.anchor: وعن محمد بن جرير أن الهاء يعود إلى الصفة لدلالة الخسران عليها وهو بعيد أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r8.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r8.claim: Another reading makes ma a relative pronoun for their deeds, with the pronoun referring back to them; its antecedent is explicit in their speech, unlike earlier readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r8.anchor: ما موصولة بمعنى التي والمراد بها الأعمال والضمير عائد إليها كأنه قيل يا حسرتنا على الأعمال الصالحة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r9.claim: Carrying their burdens is a circumstantial clause, either simultaneous with their lament or prospective; burden means sin, as Ibn Abbas reports, and the back is named because it commonly bears loads, intensifying the image of weight and pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r9.anchor: والوزر في الأصل الثقل ويقال الذنب وهو المراد هنا أي يحملون ذنوبهم وخطاياهم كما روي عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r10.claim: The burden on the back is a representative metaphor for the severe hardship and punishment their sins bring; another view takes the carrying literally because deeds take bodily form.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r10.anchor: والمراد بيان سوء حالهم وشدة ما يجدونه من المشقة والآلام والعقوبات العظيمة بسبب الذنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r11.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r11.claim: Al-Suddi describes an evil deed taking the form of an ugly, foul companion in the grave, then mounting its owner at resurrection and driving him to the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r11.anchor: ليس من رجل ظالم يموت فيدخل قبره إلا جاءه رجل قبيح الوجه أسود اللون منتن الريح عليه ثياب دنسة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r12.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r12.claim: Amr ibn Qays says a believer is met by his good deed in a beautiful, fragrant form, which reminds him that it carried him in worldly life and now he should ride it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r12.anchor: إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله عمله في أحسن شيء صورة وأطيبه ريحا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r13.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r13.claim: In the same report, the unbeliever meets his foul deed, which says that it used to ride him in life and will ride him now.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r13.anchor: كذلك كنت في الدنيا أنا عملك السيء طالما ركبتني في الدنيا فانا اليوم أركبك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r14.claim: Some interpret all such descriptions figuratively, but the author sees no obstacle to their literal sense and notes that many Sunnis hold that deeds are embodied in the next world, as the apparent weighing language suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p132/r14.anchor: وبعضهم يجعل كل ما ورد في هذا الباب مما ذكر تمثيلا أيضا ولا مانع من الحمل على الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r1.claim: The closing phrase completes and reinforces the preceding warning; 'sa'a' may be a transitive verb meaning how bad their burden is, with ma as relative, verbal noun, or indefinite subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r1.anchor: تذييل مقرر لما قبله وتكملة له و ( ساء ) تحتمل كما قيل هنا ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أن تكون المتعدية المتصرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r2.claim: Alternatively sa'a is made intransitive and takes an exclamatory force: how awful is what they carry, or their burden.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r2.anchor: أنها حولت إلى فعل اللازم بضم العين واشربت معنى التعجب والمعنى ما أسوأ الذي يزرونه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r3.claim: A third analysis treats sa'a as intensified blame, equal in meaning and grammatical behavior to bi's.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p133/r3.anchor: حولت أيضا للمبالغة في الذم فتساوي بئس في المعنى والأحكام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r1.claim: Those who deny meeting God lose themselves by denying resurrection and return to God after death; the Hour is resurrection and comes suddenly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r1.anchor: أي: خسروا أنفسهم بتكذيبهم المصير إلى الله بالبعث بعد الموت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r2.claim: Ḥasrat is an intensified vocative for regret; Sibawayh explains it as addressing regret to say its moment has come.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r2.anchor: وقال سيبويه: كأنه يقول: أيتها الحسرة هذا أوانك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r3.claim: Farraṭnā fīhā means falling short in obedience, or leaving the deeds of the afterlife undone in worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r3.anchor: على ما فرطنا} أي: قصرنا {فيها} أي: في الطاعة، وقيل: تركنا في الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن جرير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says the pronoun refers to the transaction: they sold the afterlife for this world, and the mention of the transaction is omitted because loss already implies a sale.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r4.anchor: محمد بن جرير: (1) الهاء راجعة إلى الصفقة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r5.claim: Ḥasra is intense remorse, likened to a traveler whose mount fails during a long journey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r5.anchor: والحسرة شدة الندم، حتى يتحسر النادم، كما يتحسر الذي تقوم به دابته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r6.claim: Awzār means burdens and sins; the sinners carry them on their backs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r7.speaker: السدي وغيره
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r7.claim: A believer's beautiful, fragrant good deed greets him at resurrection and carries him, while a disbeliever's foul deed rides him after having been ridden by him in life; this explains carrying sins on backs and being gathered mounted.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r8.claim: He glosses the closing phrase as condemning the load they carry: what a wretched burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p138#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بئس الحمل حملوا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r1.claim: Those denying meeting God lose blessings and earn lasting punishment; meeting God means resurrection and what follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r1.anchor: إذ فاتهم النعم واستوجبوا العذاب المقيم ولقاء الله البعث وما يتبعه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r2.claim: The Hour clause ends their denial, not their loss, which has no end; baghtah may be a circumstantial adverb or verbal noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r2.anchor: غاية لكذبوا لا لخسر، لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له. { بغتة } فجأة ونصبها على الحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r3.claim: Their cry summons their regret because its time has come; they regret negligence in worldly life, understood though unmentioned, or negligence about the Hour and belief in it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r3.anchor: قصرنا { فيها } في الحياة الدنيا أضمرت وإن لم يجر ذكرها للعلم بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r4.claim: Carrying burdens on their backs depicts their deserved sins; the following phrase condemns their load.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:31-32/r4.anchor: تمثيل لاستحقاقهم آصار الآثام. { ألا ساء ما يزرون } بئس شيئا يزرونه وزرهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r1.claim: Those who deny meeting God lose every reward they might have secured, and their denial continues until the Hour arrives.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r1.anchor: قد خسروا كل شيء يمكن إحرازه من الثواب العظيم واستمر تكذيبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r2.claim: The Hour includes death as its beginning, since everyone who dies has reached his own Hour.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r2.anchor: وكذا الموت الذي هو مبدأها فإن من مات جاءت ساعته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r3.claim: Its arrival is sudden: people cannot know the precise time it will come, even in a general way.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r3.anchor: أو بغتتهم بإتيانها على حين غفلة , لا يمكن أن يشعروا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r4.claim: Calling on regret as if summoning a companion is a metaphor that magnifies their remorse and warns people to avoid its causes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r4.anchor: أي تعالى احضرينا أيها الحسرة اللائقة بنا في هذا المقام !

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r5.claim: Their regret is for neglecting what would benefit them in the afterlife: disciplining the soul and following the messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r5.anchor: ففاتنا ما يسعد فيها من تهذيب الأخلاق المهيئة للسباق بترك اتباع الرسل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r6.claim: God gave people outward senses and bodily faculties, inward reason and thought, and prophets with miracles so they could acquire lasting knowledge and virtue; they squandered these tools on fleeting pleasures.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625/r6.anchor: وأفاض عليه نعما ظاهرة وهي الحواس الظاهرة المدركة والأعضاء والآلات الجثمانية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.claim: The sinners carry their sins as heavy loads on their backs; their deeds may be embodied as burdens, and the image conveys a horror beyond human comprehension.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يجسد أعمالهم أجسادا ثقالا , فيكلفوا حملها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.claim: The emphatic rebuke gathers up the many defects of this burden and its unbearable weight.

DURR-FULL:v3p262/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الحسرة الندامة

DURR-FULL:v3p262/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r4.claim: The Prophet explains the regret as Hell’s people seeing their former homes in Paradise; the compiler identifies the report’s chain as sound.
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {يا حسرتنا

DURR-FULL:v3p262/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r5.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the cry as regret and neglecting deeds for Paradise, then reports that a wicked person’s ugly, foul deed appears in the grave and ultimately carries him to Hell as the burden on his back.
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r5.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {يا حسرتنا} قال: ندامتنا {على ما فرطنا فيها} قال: ضيعنا من عمل الجنة

DURR-FULL:v3p262/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r6.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الملائي
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r6.claim: A believer’s good deed appears beautiful and fragrant and tells him to ride it in the afterlife, as he rode it in life; the report cites 19:85.
DURR-FULL:v3p262/r6.anchor: عن عمرو بن قيس الملائي قال: إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله عمله في أحسن صورة

DURR-FULL:v3p263/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r1.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الملائي
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r1.claim: The unbeliever’s foul and ugly deed tells him that it will ride him now, as he rode it in worldly life, illustrating the burden on their backs.
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r1.anchor: وإن الكافر يستقبله أقبح شيء صورة وأنتنه ريحا فيقول: هل تعرفني

DURR-FULL:v3p263/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r2.speaker: أبو مرزوق
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r2.claim: Abu Marzuq transmits a similar account through ‘Amr ibn Qays about a person’s deed accompanying him after death.

DURR-FULL:v3p263/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r3.claim: The phrase ‘how evil is what they carry’ means their deeds.
DURR-FULL:v3p263/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ألا ساء ما يزرون} قال: ما يعملون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p103/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p103/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p103/r2.claim: To compare the Qurʾānic uses of jāʾa and atā, the author cautions against extracting a phrase: read each entire verse and its context, including the differing accounts of the Hour in 6:31 and 6:40–41.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p103/r2.anchor: لا يصح اقتطاع جزء من الآية للاستدلال، بل ينبغي النظرُ في الآية كلها وفي السياق أيضاً ليصحَّ الاستدلالُ والحكم.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p82/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p82/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p82/r1.claim: Ghafir describes peoples who mocked messengers and only believed on seeing God's punishment, too late for their faith to help. He says verb comparisons require reading the whole verse and context; this passage introduces, but does not finish, the comparison of جاء and أتى.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p82/r1.anchor: لا يصح اقتطاع جزء من الآية للاستدلال، بل ينبغي النظرُ في الآية كلها وفي السياق أيضا

BURHAN:v1p93/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p93/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p93/r3.claim: The ending yazirūn echoes awzārahum as paronomasia; backs are named rather than heads because they bear weight better, evoking the burden of sins.
BURHAN:v1p93/r3.anchor: لأن الظهر أقوى للحمل فأشار إلى ثقل الأوزار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r1.claim: The Hour's arrival in the afterlife for deniers is the harder, more grievous scene and takes jāʾa; the worldly appeal, where God may lift what is invoked, takes atā.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r1.anchor: فالموقف الأول أشق وأشد مما في الثانية، فجاء بالفعل (جاء) لما هو أصعب وأشق. ويستعمل (أتى) لما هو أخف وأيسر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r2.claim: The author argues that jāʾa is morphologically heavier: the Qur'an uses only its past form, whereas atā occurs in past, present, imperative, and participial forms, matching heavier and lighter scenes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r2.anchor: الفعل (جاء) أثقل من (أتى) في اللفظ بدليل أنه لم يرد في القرآن فعل مضارع لـ (جاء)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r1.claim: Jāʾat is used for the harsher arrival of the Resurrection, while atat is used for the lighter worldly crisis from which God may rescue people if He wills.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r1.anchor: فالموقف الأول أشق وأشد مما في الثانية، فجاء بالفعل (جاء) دون (أتى) بخلاف الآية الثانية.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r2.claim: The first passage depicts deniers at the afterlife, remorseful and bearing their burdens; the second is worldly, as people call on God and He may remove their affliction, unlike in the afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r2.anchor: فإن الأولى في الآخرة وفي الذين كذبوا باليوم الآخر، وهم نادمون متحسرون على ما فرطوا في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r3.claim: The general pattern is jāʾa for what is difficult and severe, and ata for what is easier and lighter.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r3.anchor: فاتضح أن القرآن إنما يستعمل (جاء) لما هو أصعب وأشق. ويستعمل (أتى) لما هو أخف وأيسر.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r4.claim: Jāʾa is heavier in sound and, the author says, appears in the Qur'an only in the past form, unlike ata in multiple conjugations; the heavier word suits the harder scene.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p83/r4.anchor: ولعل من أسباب ذلك أن الفعل (جاء) أثقل من (أتى) في اللفظ
